name: pin-progress
summary: A section that pins while the scrollbar drives a 3D card stack through a flip: the stack turns rotateY -180 to 0, every spinner unwinds a full turn, and the cards rise and land.

sync.description: How closely the timeline tracks the scrollbar. Upstream's onScroll sync.

enter.description: Where the pinned range starts, as element/container edges. Upstream's onScroll enter.

leave.description: Where the pinned range ends, as element/container edges. Upstream's onScroll leave.

deviations.what: The .fx-pin__spinner wrappers are in snippet.html instead of being created and inserted around each card at runtime.
deviations.why: Two reasons. The CSS resting state has to position them, which it cannot do for elements that only exist once the script has run; and destroy() becomes a revert rather than an unwrap, so tearing a section down cannot leave rearranged DOM behind.

deviations.what: debug: true on the scroll observer is off.
deviations.why: It draws anime's scroll-range rulers over the page. That is an example looking at itself, not something a generated site should ship.

deviations.what: Each spinner carries a small `top` offset in CSS (0, 10, 20, 30, 40px).
deviations.why: The timeline's end state is a perfect overlap -- rotate 0 and rotateZ at a multiple of -360 -- so with nothing else the landed deck reads as a single card. The offset is a layout property, not a transform, so anime's inline transforms compose with it and neither state is disturbed.

deviations.what: Selectors are ours (.fx-pin__card, .fx-pin__spinner, .fx-pin__stack, .fx-pin__face--front/--back, .fx-pin__track for upstream's .card, .spinner, .stack, .front, .back, .sticky-container) and targets are passed as elements.
deviations.why: The example owns its whole page; an effect is one section among several and may appear twice on a page. Passing the elements the section actually holds is what keeps two mounts independent.

deviations.what: The CSS resting state is the timeline's end state rather than the section being blank until the observer fires.
deviations.why: Effect contract: the section has to look finished on CSS alone. A pinned reveal whose observer never runs must not leave the cards invisible.

deviations.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion nothing is set, animated or observed.
deviations.why: Effect contract: mount() stays at rest, and the resting deck is already the finished content.
